source.title: Dynamical Isometry: The Missing Ingredient for Neural Network Pruning
source.authors: Huan Wang; Can Qin; Yue Bai; Y. Fu

record.file_problem: Full text supplied; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: Uses dynamical isometry to motivate and evaluate a pruning recovery method, reporting pruning and fine-tuning results. It does not test the listed claims about training error from random initialization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports Jacobian singular values and test accuracy for pruned and fine-tuned networks, not training classification error for the claim's settings. Its initialization and optimization findings concern pruning inherited weights, so they do not test a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study uses dynamical isometry to explain pruning and evaluate recovery methods. Its own results concern Jacobian singular values and test accuracy during fine-tuning of inherited weights. It does not compare activation-matched initializations for training speed or trainable depth, or directly test another listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that pruning damages dynamical isometry, fine-tuning can recover it, and larger learning rates can accelerate recovery. They attribute pruning-versus-scratch results to fine-tuning schedules and report pruning advantages in most comparisons. They also conclude that OrthP's effectiveness on nonlinear and convolutional networks remains unsatisfactory.
record.recipe_differences: Studies orthogonalization and fine-tuning of pruned pretrained networks, rather than gradient training from random initialization to training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with pruning ratio, initial learning rate, fine-tuning duration, network type, and use of OrthP.

fits_no_version.finding: Structured pruning decreases mean Jacobian singular values. In the linear MLP, OrthP improves early test accuracy and largely removes the final-accuracy advantage of the larger learning-rate schedule; longer fine-tuning also reduces that advantage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The starting weights and fine-tuning schedule affect recovery of structured-pruned networks, with dynamical-isometry recovery proposed as an explanation.

record.problems: The central initialization analysis uses a toy linear MLP; the authors say OrthP does not work well on networks of greater practical interest. The reported accuracy tables measure test accuracy rather than training error. Some JSV results are figure-only.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported test-accuracy comparisons, including Tables 4–7, were left out because they concern pruning versus scratch-training performance and do not measure the claim's training-error outcome. Figure 2's per-epoch curves are also figure-only and do not report training classification error.

untested.parts: Training classification error from random initialization on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and model-size or regularization effects.
Spurious local minima and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation across depth, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the specified plain-network and normalization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh initialization; extremely deep orthogonal convolutional networks.
Loss recovery above an initial stability threshold, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Controlled batch-normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The exclusion is specific to the listed versions: V4 concerns initialization effects on optimization, so lack of training classification error alone would not exclude it. Here the comparisons concern inherited pruned weights and recovery-method performance, without testing V4's specified initialization or depth comparisons. Mean Jacobian singular value is also insufficient to establish that the full singular-value spectrum concentrates near one.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and the stated CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 settings.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and spurious local minima.
Plain versus residual networks across depth, and the stated normalization and initialization settings.
Activation-matched random initializations, signal and gradient propagation across depth, and the stated orthogonal initialization comparisons.
Training above the stability threshold and sharpness behavior.
Batch normalization comparisons and the stated datasets and architectures.
